rules.title: Trust the broad market over the index
rules.rule: When bonds, currencies, commodities and volatility disagree with the equity index, trust them; when stocks and oil disagree, trust oil.

sources.statement: When bonds, currencies, commodities and volatility disagree with the equity index, trust the broader market over the index; when stocks and oil disagree, trust oil.

rules.title: Tops roll over in sequence
rules.rule: Spot a top as small names, then megacaps, then manufacturers, then equipment makers roll over in sequence.

sources.statement: Spot a top by watching small names, then megacaps, then manufacturers, then equipment makers roll over in sequence.

rules.title: Bonds fail as hedge in inflation shocks
rules.rule: In high-inflation regimes and energy supply shocks, expect bonds to fall with stocks and favor gold and energy as hedges.

sources.statement: In high-inflation regimes and energy supply shocks, expect bonds to fall with stocks rather than hedge them; favor gold and energy instead.

rules.title: Avoid duration in a bear steepener
rules.rule: In a bear steepener, avoid long-duration bonds, utilities, consumer staples and real estate.

sources.statement: In a bear steepener, avoid long-duration bonds, utilities, consumer staples and real estate.

rules.title: Classify oil moves as demand or supply
rules.rule: Classify an oil move as demand-driven or supply-driven before judging its effect on bonds and the portfolio.

sources.statement: Classify an oil move as demand-driven or supply-driven before judging its effect on bonds and the portfolio.

rules.title: Oil supply shock rule of thumb
rules.rule: Estimate an oil supply shock as roughly a 4% price rise for every 1% of supply lost.

sources.statement: Estimate an oil supply shock as roughly a 4% price rise for every 1% of supply lost.

rules.title: Energy spikes favor USD over EUR
rules.rule: When oil or gas spikes, favor the dollar over the euro because Europe imports its energy.

sources.statement: When oil or gas spikes, favor the dollar over the euro because Europe imports its energy.

rules.title: Energy inflation traps central banks
rules.rule: Expect a central bank to be trapped when energy lifts inflation while growth weakens; hikes do not cure energy inflation.

sources.statement: Expect a central bank to be trapped when energy pushes inflation up while growth weakens; rate hikes do not cure energy inflation.

rules.title: The unpriced outcome is the surprise
rules.rule: When one outcome is heavily priced, treat the opposite outcome as the bigger surprise the market must unprice.

sources.statement: When one outcome is heavily priced, treat the opposite outcome as the bigger surprise the market must unprice.

rules.title: Don't buy a liquidity crisis early
rules.rule: Do not buy into a liquidity crisis until volatility comes down; expect forced margin selling even in assets like gold.

sources.statement: Do not buy into a liquidity crisis until volatility comes down; expect forced margin selling even in assets like gold.

rules.title: No Fed put while inflation runs hot
rules.rule: Do not count on a Fed put while six-month inflation runs above the 12-month rate and most components exceed 3%.

sources.statement: Do not count on a Fed put while six-month inflation runs above the 12-month rate and most components exceed 3%.

rules.title: Judge a rate cut by its reason
rules.rule: Judge a rate cut by why it was needed, not as good news by itself.

sources.statement: Judge a rate cut by why it was needed, not as good news by itself.

rules.title: Favor cash when bills out-yield stocks
rules.rule: Compare T-bill yields with equity dividend yields and favor cash when bills pay far more.

sources.statement: Compare T-bill yields with equity dividend yields and favor cash when bills pay far more.

rules.title: Pick CSP names by IV, chart and trigger
rules.rule: Choose cash-secured put candidates with high implied volatility, a clear chart structure and a fundamental or macro trigger.

sources.statement: Choose cash-secured put candidates with high implied volatility, a clear chart structure and a fundamental or macro trigger.

rules.title: Covered calls are not downside protection
rules.rule: Use covered calls only with a sideways to moderately bullish view and willingness to sell at the strike, not as downside protection.

sources.statement: Use covered calls only with a sideways to moderately bullish view and willingness to sell at the strike; they are not downside protection.

rules.title: Sell condors after VIX calms
rules.rule: Sell iron condors only once VIX has calmed back down after a spike.

sources.statement: Sell iron condors only once VIX has calmed back down after a spike.

rules.title: Manage debit spread legs together
rules.rule: In a debit spread, accept that the debit can be lost and profit is capped, and manage both legs together.

sources.statement: In a debit put spread, accept that the debit can be lost and profit is capped, and manage both legs together.

rules.title: Trade observed flows, not expectations
rules.rule: Trade the flows you see, not your expectations.

sources.statement: Trade the flows you see, not your expectations.

rules.title: Follow the price of money, not Fed guesses
rules.rule: Do not try to predict the Fed; follow what markets price for rates.

sources.statement: Do not try to predict the Fed; follow the price of money.

rules.title: Analyze from macro down to the stock
rules.rule: Analyze top down: macro, regional markets, sector, peers, then the stock.

sources.statement: Analyze top down: macro, regional markets, sector, peers, then the stock.
Find the sector rotation: start from the indices, then the strongest sectors, then the best setups inside those sectors.
Pick long-term stocks top-down: choose the sector first, then screen companies on metrics such as P/E and debt-to-equity rather than analysing one company at a time.
Check the stock's sector and the overall market before entering (e.g. skip a sector name ahead of the sector leader's earnings).

rules.title: Seek an information edge on flows
rules.rule: Seek an edge by knowing more or knowing earlier, especially about who is buying and selling.

sources.statement: Seek an information edge by knowing more or knowing earlier, especially about who is buying and selling.

rules.title: Match data dates and components
rules.rule: Match observation dates and periods, and separate components such as real yields and breakevens, before comparing data.

sources.statement: Match observation dates and periods, and separate components such as real yields and breakevens, before comparing or acting on data.

rules.title: Own bullion, not miners, for gold
rules.rule: Do not use gold mining stocks as a substitute for gold; confirm the fund owns bullion.

sources.statement: Do not use gold mining stocks as a substitute for gold; check the fund factsheet confirms you own bullion.

rules.title: Check cash flow behind earnings
rules.rule: Check that free cash flow after capex keeps pace with earnings and can fund dividends and buildouts without fresh debt.

sources.statement: Read the cash flow line before the earnings headline: compute cash after capex for the same period and check that it keeps pace with reported earnings.
Check that free cash flow, not just accounting earnings, can fund the dividend.
Ask whether a capex buildout is funded from own cash flow or fresh debt, and whether free cash flow holds as capex rises.

rules.title: Stress-test income without specials
rules.rule: Separate earnings-linked dividends from special payments and stress-test income without the special part.

sources.statement: Separate earnings-linked dividends from special payments and stress-test your income forecast without the special component.

rules.title: Check refinancing costs on debt
rules.rule: Check a company's debt maturities and the cost of replacing old debt, since higher interest cuts payouts.

sources.statement: Check a company's debt maturities and compare old rates with replacement rates, since higher interest reduces cash for payouts.

rules.title: Extra yield is pay for extra risk
rules.rule: Before reaching for yield, check spread, duration, fiscal and inflation risk, currency and hedging cost, and compare with safe deposits.

sources.statement: Before reaching for yield, check spread, duration, fiscal risk, inflation exposure and currency; extra yield is pay for extra risk.
Before buying a high-yield foreign asset, check the coupon against local inflation, the currency move and the hedging cost, and calculate total return in your own currency.
Skip a property investment whose yield is no better than bank deposits, even in a top location.

rules.title: Check EPS against dilution and buybacks
rules.rule: Before celebrating EPS growth, check total profit growth, diluted share count and the price paid for buybacks.

sources.statement: Before celebrating EPS growth, check total profit growth, the diluted share count and the price paid for buybacks.

rules.title: Stress-test valuation with lower earnings
rules.rule: Cut your earnings assumption and recalculate whether you would still pay today's price.

sources.statement: Cut your earnings assumption and recalculate whether you would still pay today's price.

rules.title: Judge sovereign debt by growth vs rates
rules.rule: Judge sovereign debt by nominal growth versus borrowing costs, primary balance, maturity profile and currency, not the debt ratio alone.

sources.statement: Judge sovereign debt by nominal growth versus borrowing costs, primary balance, maturity profile and currency, not the debt ratio alone.

rules.title: Compounded QQQ/NDX gamma levels
rules.rule: Give top priority to zones where the QQQ and NDX gamma maps both show large exposure at the same time.

sources.statement: Give top priority to compounded levels, where the QQQ and NDX gamma maps show large exposure in the same zone at the same time.

rules.title: Gamma nodes on VIX
rules.rule: Mark positive gamma nodes on VIX as support and resistance and read them inversely for SPX and NQ: VIX rejecting lower from a node supports higher indices.

sources.statement: Mark positive gamma nodes on VIX: they tend to hold as support and resistance, and VIX moves opposite to SPX, so a VIX rejection lower supports higher indices.
When VIX rejects lower from its main negative-gamma strike in your plan, expect indices to rise.

rules.title: Falling VIX favors longs (vanna)
rules.rule: Check VIX direction before trading index futures: falling VIX forces dealer buying, so lean long; rising VIX makes longs riskier.

sources.statement: Check VIX each morning before NQ: falling VIX forces dealer buying (vanna), so lean long; rising VIX makes longs riskier.

rules.title: Charm as a slow directional wind
rules.rule: Use charm (delta decay) as a supportive or suppressive lean that grows into the afternoon and pulls price toward key gamma levels; it never triggers a trade by itself.

sources.statement: Expect charm to pull NQ toward the nearest key gamma level in the afternoon; in the first 90 minutes charm barely matters.
Use the charm surface for the day's lean (supportive or suppressive) and its strength; charm supports or suppresses a move but never triggers a trade.

rules.title: Check regime before blaming yourself
rules.rule: When a working setup suddenly stops working, first check whether the volatility regime changed before blaming yourself or changing the strategy.

sources.statement: When a working setup suddenly gets chopped up, first check whether the market regime (volatility) changed before blaming yourself or tweaking the strategy.
A strategy that stops working may be suffering a regime change rather than being bad.

rules.title: Gamma is not a direction call
rules.rule: Read a gamma level as a place where price will react if it arrives, and gamma sign as pinning vs acceleration, never as a buy or sell signal or a price forecast.

sources.statement: Read a gamma exposure level as a place where price will react if it arrives, not as a forecast that price will go there.
Do not read gamma sign as a trade direction: negative gamma is not a sell signal and positive gamma is not a buy signal; positive gamma pins only at the biggest strikes, negative gamma accelerates.

rules.title: Choose GEX data source by product
rules.rule: Use exchange-tagged gamma data (real signs, SPX and VIX only) for SPX context and consolidated multi-exchange open-interest data (complete, assumed signs) for QQQ, NDX and stock levels.

sources.statement: Pick GEX data by product: CBOE-tagged data has real signs but covers only SPX and VIX; consolidated multi-exchange data covers QQQ, NDX and stocks but with assumed signs and more noise.
As an NQ trader, build the level map from open-interest gamma on QQQ and NDX (complete coverage) and use SPX tagged data for broad context; ES traders should use SPX tagged data directly.

rules.title: Dealer delta exposure for daily bias
rules.rule: Set the daily bias from dealer net delta exposure (and its put/call ratio) before layering gamma regime, charm and gamma levels.

sources.statement: Build the daily bias from dealer delta exposure and its put/call ratio before using gamma levels for location.
Read net delta for dealer positioning first, then the gamma surface (positive mean-reverting, negative amplifying) and charm surface (supportive or suppressive), and only then add gamma levels.

rules.title: Treat gamma levels as zones
rules.rule: Treat a gamma exposure level as a zone, not an exact price.

sources.statement: Treat a gamma exposure level as a zone, not an exact price.

rules.title: Written pre-market plan with scenarios
rules.rule: Before every session, write a plan with macro context, options positioning, key levels and two or three scenarios, and later check whether it played out.

sources.statement: Spend about 15 minutes before every session on macro context, earnings, the options matrix, gamma and delta exposure shifts and key levels; know the plan before the bell.
Write the pre-market plan down daily and later check whether what you expected actually happened.
Build the trade narrative from several price drivers (gamma levels, volatility, macro, sectors) and plan two or three scenarios before the open.

rules.title: Check equal-weight before calling washout
rules.rule: Before calling a washout in a cap-weighted index, check equal-weight and constituent moving-average participation for megacap divergence.

sources.statement: Before calling a washout in a cap-weighted index, check equal-weight (RSP) and constituent-level moving-average participation for megacap divergence.

rules.title: Range-bound structures in positive gamma
rules.rule: In positive dealer-gamma regimes, prefer near-the-money range-bound defined-risk structures over far out-of-the-money momentum bets.

sources.statement: In positive-gamma regimes, prefer range-bound defined-risk structures near the money over far out-of-the-money momentum bets.

rules.title: Size conservatively in negative gamma
rules.rule: In negative-gamma regimes, size conservatively, avoid tight intraday stops, and prefer defined-risk or longer-dated options.

sources.statement: In negative-gamma regimes, size conservatively, do not rely on tight intraday stops, and prefer defined-risk spreads or longer-dated options that survive whipsaws.

rules.title: Distrust naive GEX in flow regimes
rules.rule: Distrust naive GEX during retail call-buying waves or customer put selling, because the assumed dealer sign flips.

sources.statement: Distrust naive GEX during retail call-buying waves or customer put selling, because the assumed dealer sign flips and the regime reading inverts.

rules.title: Classify IV inversions event vs systemic
rules.rule: Before acting on an IV inversion, classify it: event-driven inversions collapse on the event date, while systemic-stress inversions can last days or weeks with high realized volatility, so do not assume an immediate peak.

sources.statement: Classify an IV inversion before acting: an event-driven inversion (catalyst inside the front expiry) collapses on the event date, while a systemic one can persist for days or weeks.
Expect a systemic-stress inversion to stay inverted for days or weeks while realized volatility stays high; do not assume an immediate volatility peak.

rules.title: Avoid front-month longs when VIX/VIX3M above 1
rules.rule: Avoid buying front-month single-leg calls or puts when VIX/VIX3M is above 1.0, because you pay peak implied volatility.

sources.statement: Avoid buying front-month single-leg calls or puts when VIX/VIX3M is above 1.0, because you pay peak implied volatility.

rules.title: Go longer-dated during IV inversion
rules.rule: During an IV term-structure inversion, prefer longer-dated defined-risk structures, which suffer less vega crush when the curve normalizes.

sources.statement: During an IV inversion, prefer longer-dated defined-risk structures, since back-end IV is less inflated and suffers less vega crush when the curve normalizes.

rules.title: Short index only as tactical hedge
rules.rule: Short the index only as a tactical portfolio hedge, never as a long-run bet against it.

sources.statement: Short the index only as a tactical hedge for the portfolio, never as a long-run bet against it.

rules.title: Nasdaq failed breakout is red flag
rules.rule: Treat a failed Nasdaq 100 breakout as a first red flag and reduce risk or hedge.

sources.statement: Treat a failed breakout in the Nasdaq 100 as a first red flag to reduce risk or hedge.

rules.title: Skip dip if leader fails demand
rules.rule: Do not buy the dip when the strongest sector fails to attract buyers at a key demand zone during a selloff.

sources.statement: When the market's strongest sector fails to attract buyers at a key demand zone during a selloff, do not buy the dip.

rules.title: Scale in gradually when VIX is extreme
rules.rule: When VIX is above about 35, add to long-term positions gradually and keep cash for lower prices.

sources.statement: When volatility is extreme (VIX above 35), start adding to long-term positions gradually instead of going all in, and keep cash for lower prices.

rules.title: Exit IPO proxy before listing
rules.rule: When trading a listed proxy for an upcoming IPO, exit before the IPO debuts because proxies tend to peak before listing.

sources.statement: When trading a listed proxy for an upcoming IPO, plan to exit before the IPO debuts, because proxies tend to peak before the listing.

rules.title: PCE print drives growth stocks
rules.rule: Read a hotter PCE print as a headwind and a cooler print as a tailwind for high-valuation growth stocks.

sources.statement: Treat a hotter PCE inflation print as a headwind for high-valuation growth stocks and a cooler print as a tailwind.

rules.title: Oil supply spikes rotate sectors
rules.rule: When oil rises on supply-risk premium, favour oil producers and expect airlines, transport and cruise lines to suffer most.

sources.statement: When oil rises on supply-risk premium, expect oil producers to win and airlines, transport and cruise lines to be hit hardest.

rules.title: Index inclusion plus high short interest
rules.rule: Look for setups combining forced index-inclusion buying, short interest above 20% and a building catalyst.

sources.statement: Look for setups that combine forced index-inclusion buying, short interest above 20% and a building catalyst narrative.

rules.title: Buy strong stocks sold after good earnings
rules.rule: Consider buying a fundamentally strong stock that sold off after a strong earnings quarter.

sources.statement: Consider buying a fundamentally strong stock that sold off after a strong earnings quarter as a cleaner entry.

rules.title: High SOFR signals funding stress
rules.rule: Treat a high SOFR as funding stress and a risk-off signal.

sources.statement: Treat a high SOFR as funding stress and a risk-off signal.

rules.title: Big VIX spike signals exhaustion
rules.rule: Read a big VIX spike as likely panic exhaustion, since professionals have usually already hedged.

sources.statement: Read a big VIX spike as likely exhaustion: most of the time the panic is behind us because professionals have already hedged.

rules.title: Low VIX is not safety
rules.rule: Do not read a quiet, low VIX as safety, because selling can happen unseen.

sources.statement: Do not read a quiet, low VIX as safety; selling can be happening unseen.

rules.title: Review scheduled events before the open
rules.rule: Before the US open, check the day's scheduled events such as earnings releases and Fed actions.

sources.statement: Before the US open, review the day's scheduled events: earnings releases and Fed actions.

rules.title: Treat Jackson Hole speech as event risk
rules.rule: Treat the Jackson Hole Fed chair speech as a market-moving event, because a single hawkish or dovish line can move the market sharply.

sources.statement: Treat the Jackson Hole Fed chair speech as a market-moving event, since a single hawkish or dovish line has moved the market sharply.

rules.title: Watch short yields for Fed
rules.rule: Anticipate Fed policy by watching Treasury yields from 3-month bills to 2-year notes.

sources.statement: To anticipate Fed policy, watch short-term Treasury yields from 3-month bills to 2-year notes.

rules.title: Pick pairs from same sector
rules.rule: Build pair candidates from economically linked stocks in the same sector or industry before testing, and prefer cointegration over correlation.

sources.statement: Build the pairs universe from same-sector, same-industry stocks rather than testing every available stock.
Select pair candidates with an economic basis (e.g., same sector) before testing cointegration; prefer cointegration over correlation.

rules.title: Explainable economic link for pairs
rules.rule: Only trade a pair whose economic link you can explain in plain terms without statistics.

sources.statement: Only trade a pair whose economic link you can explain in plain terms without statistics or math.

rules.title: Pairs universe liquidity screen
rules.rule: Screen pair stocks for price of at least $50, average volume above 1 million shares, shortability and a listing history of a few years.

sources.statement: Pairs universe screen: price at least $50, average volume above 1 million shares, shortable, and listed for at least a few years.

rules.title: Regress log prices for pair spread
rules.rule: Regress the log prices of the two legs to get alpha, the hedge ratio and the spread.

sources.statement: Regress the log prices (not raw prices) of the two legs to get alpha, beta (hedge ratio) and the spread.

rules.title: Confirm cointegration with a test
rules.rule: Do not judge a spread by eye; a trending spread is unlikely to be cointegrated, but confirm it with a formal test such as ADF.

sources.statement: Do not rely on an eyeballed spread; a visibly trending spread is unlikely to be cointegrated, but confirm with the test.

rules.title: Use rolling Kalman hedge ratio
rules.rule: Replace a constant cointegration beta with a rolling (Kalman filter) hedge ratio, because pairs drift in and out of cointegration.

sources.statement: Replace the constant Engle-Granger beta with a rolling hedge ratio (Kalman filter) because pairs move in and out of cointegration.

rules.title: Check hedge ratio stability for pairs
rules.rule: Even if a pair tests cointegrated, check the (Kalman) hedge ratio; if it trends or flips rather than staying stable, treat the pair as unreliable.

sources.statement: The hedge ratio should stay roughly stable or mean revert; a trending hedge ratio means the pair relationship is changing.
Even when a long-window test says cointegrated, check the Kalman hedge ratio; if the relationship has flipped, treat the pair as unreliable.

rules.title: HMM detects pair regime change
rules.rule: Use a hidden Markov model on spread, volatility or returns to detect when a pair falls out of cointegration.

sources.statement: Use a hidden Markov model on spread, volatility or returns to detect whether a pair has fallen out of cointegration (regime change).

rules.title: Trade spread band crossings
rules.rule: When the spread crosses above the upper band go long X and short Y, and when it crosses below the lower band go short X and long Y.

sources.statement: When the spread crosses above the upper bound go long X and short Y; when it crosses below the lower bound go short X and long Y.

rules.title: Exit pair near spread mean
rules.rule: Close a pairs trade when the spread returns near its mean, using an inner exit bound about half a standard deviation from the mean.

sources.statement: Pairs exit: close when the spread comes back near the mean (exit bounds about half a standard deviation from the mean).
Exit the pair when the spread approaches the mean, the inner exit bound.

rules.title: Denoise the spread before signalling
rules.rule: Consider denoising the spread, for example with a wavelet low-pass, so small noisy moves do not trigger trades.

sources.statement: Consider denoising the spread (e.g. wavelet low-pass) so small noisy moves do not trigger trade signals.

rules.title: Trade a portfolio of many pairs
rules.rule: Never trade a single pair; run many pairs so individual cointegration breakdowns average out.

sources.statement: Never trade a single pair; run a portfolio of many pairs so cointegration breakdowns average out.

rules.title: Long cointegration rarely persists
rules.rule: Do not assume cointegration holds over five-year lookbacks, because it rarely lasts that long.

sources.statement: Five-year cointegration is uncommon; cointegration usually does not last that long.

rules.title: HMM regimes as filter only
rules.rule: Use hidden Markov regime estimates as a pre-trade filter, not as a standalone trading signal.

sources.statement: Use hidden Markov regime estimates as a pre-trade filter, not as a trading signal on their own.

rules.title: Define concrete rules before testing
rules.rule: Write concrete, testable entry, exit and trigger rules before looking at any results.

sources.statement: Write entry, exit and trigger rules before looking at any results to avoid overfitting and look-ahead bias.
Convert vague ideas into concrete testable rules before backtesting (e.g., "small gap down" -> gap between -1% and -2%).

rules.title: Every strategy needs explicit risk limits
rules.rule: Give every strategy explicit risk management such as maximum position sizes, stop losses or exposure limits.

sources.statement: Every strategy needs explicit risk management: maximum position sizes, stop losses or exposure limits.

rules.title: Use penalized regression for correlated features
rules.rule: With correlated, similar features, use a penalized fit such as ridge regression instead of OLS.

sources.statement: Fight overfitting: correlated, similar features plus OLS overfit noise; prefer a penalized fit such as ridge regression.

rules.title: Match forecast and target horizons
rules.rule: Compare a forecast with a target of the same horizon.

sources.statement: Compare a forecast with a target of the same horizon (e.g. 10-day forecast vs 10-day volatility), not a mismatched one.

rules.title: Beginner core-satellite allocation
rules.rule: As a beginner, hold about 80% in an S&P 500 fund and 10% in a 2x S&P fund for full market exposure, and use only about 10% for active trading.

sources.statement: Beginner allocation: 80% S&P 500, 10% in a 2x S&P fund (SSO) for roughly full market exposure, and only 10% for active trading.

rules.title: Grow trading capital as strategies prove out
rules.rule: Increase the share of capital used for active trading only as your strategies demonstrate they work.

sources.statement: Raise the share of capital used for active trading only as your strategies prove they work.

rules.title: Inverted IV term means event
rules.rule: When 30-day implied volatility is much higher than 60-day, assume the market is pricing a near-term event.

sources.statement: If 30-day implied volatility is much higher than 60-day, the market is pricing a near-term event.

rules.title: Volatility is a surface
rules.rule: Never treat a symbol as having one volatility; specify strike and expiration and compare against the surface.

sources.statement: Never describe a symbol as having one volatility; ask which strike, which expiration, and how it compares to the surface.

rules.title: Trade the strike that breaks from neighbours
rules.rule: Do not trade the largest model-market difference; trade only a contract whose deviation breaks clearly from neighbouring strikes and is large enough to be worth it.

sources.statement: Model-vs-market options trading: do not trade the biggest model-market difference; first calibrate the model across the chain.
Trade only a contract whose model-market difference breaks clearly from the neighbouring strikes, and only if the deviation is big enough to be worth it.
You want one contract that breaks away from the options around it, not the largest raw difference.

rules.title: Target reversion to neighbours' range
rules.rule: For a pattern-break options trade, target the deviation shrinking back toward its neighbours' range rather than all the way to model price.

sources.statement: Target for a pattern-break options trade: the deviation shrinks back toward its neighbours' range, not necessarily all the way to model price.

rules.title: Model mispricing is not a trade
rules.rule: Do not treat a market price below your model price as a trade by itself.

sources.statement: The market price sitting below the model price is not by itself a trade.

rules.title: Exit when model gap turns against you
rules.rule: Exit a model-based options trade when the model price drops or the price gap starts moving against you.

sources.statement: Exit a model-based options trade when the model price drops or the gap starts moving against you.

rules.title: Risk-neutral crash odds overstate reality
rules.rule: Treat option-implied crash probabilities as possibly higher than real-world odds, because investors overpay for protection.

sources.statement: Option-implied (risk-neutral) crash probabilities can exceed real-world odds because investors overpay for protection.

rules.title: TLT put on hawkish Fed under-reaction
rules.rule: Buy a TLT put only when prediction-market Fed expectations turn more hawkish, the model expects TLT to fall, and TLT has under-reacted.

sources.statement: Rates signal: buy a TLT put only when prediction-market Fed expectations turn more hawkish, the model expects TLT to fall, and TLT has under-reacted.

rules.title: Standardize under-reaction residuals
rules.rule: Standardize the gap between the expected and actual move to judge whether an under-reaction is actually unusual.

sources.statement: Standardize the gap between expected and actual move to know whether an under-reaction is actually unusual.

rules.title: Use richer models to find mispricing
rules.rule: Look for options mispricing where a stochastic-volatility-plus-jumps model prices volatility and jump risk differently from the market.

sources.statement: Look for options mispricing where a richer model (stochastic volatility plus jumps) prices volatility and jump risk differently from the market.

rules.title: Volatility-scaled continuous forecasts
rules.rule: Express each rule as a continuous forecast proportional to expected Sharpe, scaled to an average absolute value of 10, and size positions as forecast divided by instrument volatility.

sources.statement: Express each trading rule as a continuous forecast proportional to expected Sharpe, scaled to an average absolute value of 10; size position as forecast divided by instrument volatility.

rules.title: Trend forecast as slope over volatility
rules.rule: Compute trend as the rolling OLS price slope over n days divided by volatility, giving no estimate until at least n/4 days of data exist.

sources.statement: Trend forecast = rolling OLS regression slope of price over n days divided by volatility; produce no estimate until at least n/4 days of data exist.

rules.title: Trade a family of lookbacks
rules.rule: Rather than picking one optimal parameter, trade a family of fast-to-slow parameter sets (e.g., 10-200 day windows spaced by √2) as one unit.

sources.statement: Use a set of trend lookback windows from 10 to about 200 days, spaced by factors of the square root of two, instead of one optimized window.
Instead of picking one optimal parameter, trade a family of fast-to-slow parameter sets as one unit.

rules.title: Trend lookback a fraction of trend length
rules.rule: Set the trend lookback to about one-half to one-third of the expected trend length and avoid lookbacks that are too slow.

sources.statement: Choose a trend lookback of roughly one-half to one-third of the expected trend length; a lookback that is too slow performs worst.

rules.title: Cap trading costs in Sharpe units
rules.rule: Drop rule variations whose trading costs exceed about 13 bp of Sharpe ratio per year.

sources.statement: Cap a rule variation's trading costs at 13 bp of Sharpe ratio per year; drop variations (e.g., a 5-day window) that exceed it.

rules.title: Cost per trade in risk units
rules.rule: Estimate cost per trade as commission plus half the spread, divided by volatility.

sources.statement: Estimate cost per trade in risk units as commission plus half the bid-ask spread, divided by volatility.

rules.title: Don't abandon rules on short underperformance
rules.rule: Keep a systematic rule through poor recent results, because short-run underperformance is not statistically significant.

sources.statement: Do not abandon a systematic rule because of poor recent results; short-run underperformance is not statistically significant.

rules.title: Expect strategy-type return profiles
rules.rule: Expect trend/momentum (divergent) strategies to lose small often and win big rarely, and mean-reversion (convergent) the reverse, and combine both.

sources.statement: Expect a good trend strategy to lose small amounts for long periods and earn most profit in rare large moves; do not require consistent monthly gains.
Expect mean-reversion strategies to have many small wins and rare large losses, and momentum strategies many small losses and rare large wins.
Classify strategies as divergent (right-tailed, low win rate) or convergent (high win rate, left tail) by return distribution, and combine both.

rules.title: Clean and adjust price data
rules.rule: Before analysis, check data for errors, duplicates, gaps and spikes, and use split/dividend-adjusted prices.

sources.statement: Compute returns from split/dividend-adjusted close prices; unadjusted closes show false drops on split days.
Check price data for wrong values, duplicate entries and gaps before analysis; garbage data gives garbage results.
Clean price data before use: remove spikes and adjust for corporate actions such as splits and dividends.

rules.title: ATR measures volatility, not direction
rules.rule: Measure volatility with ATR (default 14) from true range, and read rising ATR only as expanding volatility, never as a direction signal.

sources.statement: Measure volatility with ATR (default 14 periods): true range = max(high-low, |high-prev close|, |low-prev close|); rising ATR = expanding volatility, never a direction signal.

rules.title: Build portfolio across market states
rules.rule: Label periods as up, down or sideways and combine algorithms that excel in each state, keeping one that loses in a state if it adds strongly elsewhere and others cover it.

sources.statement: Label each month by S&P change: +30 points or more = strong up, -4 points or worse = down, in between = sideways; build a portfolio with 1–2 algorithms that excel in each state.
Keep an algorithm that loses in one market state (momentum lost ~$812/month in down months) if it adds strongly in other states and other algos cover that state.

rules.title: Require enough data and trades per rule
rules.rule: Require long history, many trades relative to rules and parameters, few indicators, included costs, and performance across similar instruments.

sources.statement: Robustness requirements: at least 10 years of backtest data, at least 200 trades, three or fewer indicators, slippage and commission included, coarse optimization steps.
For a daily strategy, require roughly one extra year of data for every added parameter.
Require many trades relative to the number of rules (degrees of freedom) and require the system to work across similar instruments.

rules.title: Require economic significance
rules.rule: Require economic as well as statistical significance, and reject patterns that only capture the bid-ask spread.

sources.statement: Reject scalping algorithms whose average gain per trade is close to the bid-ask spread (e.g., about $12 per ES trade).
Require economic, not just statistical, significance; a pattern that only captures the bid-ask spread is untradable.

rules.title: Commodity pairs by minimum distance
rules.rule: Pair futures within a commodity group by smallest squared normalized-price deviation over 12 months and open when the spread diverges beyond 2 standard deviations.

sources.statement: Commodity pairs: within each commodity group, pair futures by smallest sum of squared normalized-price deviations over 12 months; open when the pair diverges by more than 2 standard deviations (reported Sharpe ~1.5).

rules.title: Trade pre-earnings drift deciles
rules.rule: Go long the top decile and short the bottom decile by past earnings-announcement returns during the five days before announcements.

sources.statement: Pre-earnings drift: go long the top decile and short the bottom decile of stocks ranked by past earnings-announcement returns, holding during the five days before the announcement.

rules.title: High t-stat bar for new factors
rules.rule: Require a t-statistic of at least 3.0 for a new factor, and test it with microcaps removed and value-weighted returns.

sources.statement: Require a t-statistic of at least 3.0 (or 3.5) before accepting a new factor/anomaly; remove microcaps and value-weight returns when testing.
Require a t-statistic above 3.0, not 2.0, before believing a new factor found after multiple testing.

rules.title: Trade momentum across anomalies
rules.rule: Rank published anomalies by past performance and trade only the best-performing ones.

sources.statement: Apply momentum across published anomalies: rank anomalies by past performance and trade only the best-performing ones.

rules.title: Seek edge in research blind spots
rules.rule: Look for edge in under-researched areas such as bonds, REITs, FX, intraday and short-only, where there is less competition.

sources.statement: Look for edge in research blind spots (bonds, REITs, FX, intraday, short-only, e.g. currency-cross pairs) where less published research means less competition.

rules.title: Optimize for Sharpe, not MSE
rules.rule: Optimize models for Sharpe ratio rather than price-prediction error.

sources.statement: Optimize models for Sharpe ratio (profit divided by its volatility), not mean squared error of price prediction.

rules.title: Track record length scales with 1/Sharpe²
rules.rule: Expect proof of profitability to take about 1/Sharpe² years, so favour frequent-trading models that give more samples.

sources.statement: The time needed to demonstrate a strategy is profitable is roughly 1/Sharpe² years; low-Sharpe strategies need long track records.
Prefer models that trade frequently when judging statistical confidence; faster models produce more samples.

rules.title: RSI(2) exit on SMA closes
rules.rule: Close an RSI(2) mean-reversion long on a close above the 5-day SMA or a close below the 200-day SMA.

sources.statement: Connors RSI(2) exit: close the long on a close above the 5-day SMA, or on a close below the 200-day SMA.

rules.title: Use ML to blend alphas, not predict returns
rules.rule: Use machine learning to combine independent alpha sources or classify regimes, not to predict from raw past returns.

sources.statement: Use machine learning to blend existing independent alpha sources or for regime/style classification, not to predict from raw past returns.

rules.title: Avoid ML on small daily datasets
rules.rule: Avoid ML on daily bars, technical indicators and single series; prefer large data such as tick, order-book, fundamental, news or cross-sectional.

sources.statement: Avoid ML on daily bars, technical indicators and single futures/index series (too little data, data-snooping); prefer tick, order-book, fundamental, news or large cross-sectional data.

rules.title: Bootstrap preserving autocorrelation
rules.rule: When resampling time series, use a method that preserves serial autocorrelation.

sources.statement: When bootstrapping/bagging time-series data to reduce data-snooping bias, use a resampling method that preserves serial autocorrelation.

rules.title: Prefer feature-selecting models
rules.rule: Reduce features and prefer feature-selecting models over neural networks in non-stationary markets.

sources.statement: Reduce the number of features; prefer feature-selecting models (stepwise regression, CART, random forest) over neural networks, which fit all inputs in non-stationary markets.

rules.title: Sentiment ML long/short with 20-day hold
rules.rule: Use separate up/down classification trees on social sentiment and other factors to enter five positions daily and exit each after 20 days, expecting live results below paper.

sources.statement: Sentiment ML long/short: separate up/down classification trees on social-sentiment plus other factors; enter five positions per day and exit each after 20 days (4.7 Sharpe paper-traded; live expected lower).

rules.title: Small prediction correlation can suffice
rules.rule: Treat a prediction-to-outcome correlation around 0.12 as enough to trade profitably after costs.

sources.statement: A prediction-to-outcome correlation of about 0.12 is enough to overcome transaction costs and trade profitably.

rules.title: Regularize KNN and trees
rules.rule: Control ML overfitting with larger k or leaf sizes and normalize features for KNN.

sources.statement: Control ML overfitting with a larger k in KNN or a larger leaf size in decision trees; normalize features for KNN.

rules.title: Avoid unjustified rules and parameters
rules.rule: Keep rules few, base parameter ranges on economic rationale, and do not add indicators, stops or tuning without theory.

sources.statement: Be suspicious of complex stop-loss and trailing-stop rules added to a mediocre signal; they curve-fit the backtest and fail out of sample.
Avoid rule burden: do not keep adding entry, exit and risk rules or brute-force parameter grids; fewer rules are more robust.
Base parameter ranges on an economic rationale (e.g., volatility regimes), not wide brute-force searches.
Do not tune parameter values or add indicators without a theory behind them; that is curve fitting.

rules.title: Check factor quantile monotonicity
rules.rule: Use quantile analysis to confirm signal direction and monotonicity, flipping inverse signals.

sources.statement: Use factor quantile analysis (e.g., Alphalens) to check signal direction and monotonicity before building a strategy; flip the signal if returns run inversely.

rules.title: Warm up indicators before trading
rules.rule: Warm up indicators with history and confirm readiness before acting on signals.

sources.statement: Warm up indicators with historical data and check readiness (IsReady) before acting on their signals.

rules.title: Evaluate entries and exits separately
rules.rule: Test entries with naive exits and exits with random entries.

sources.statement: Evaluate entries separately using naive ("dumb") exits, and evaluate exits separately using random entries.

rules.title: Shorter holds tested better
rules.rule: Test shorter holding times for swing entries, since they were typically found superior to longer holds.

sources.statement: Test-derived finding: shorter holding times were typically superior to the longer holds expected for swing entries.

rules.title: Keep backup infrastructure for automation
rules.rule: Maintain backup power, internet and computer for automated trading to limit operational risk.

sources.statement: Operational risk: maintain backup power (UPS), a backup internet connection and a backup computer for automated trading.

rules.title: Combine many independent weak models
rules.rule: Combine many independent low signal-to-noise models to raise combined signal-to-noise.

sources.statement: Increase breadth across many independent bets; it scales the information ratio more cheaply than improving signal quality.
Combine many low signal-to-noise models; more independent models improve the combined signal-to-noise ratio.

rules.title: Sweep slippage to break-even
rules.rule: Sweep slippage assumptions to find the cost level at which the strategy stops being profitable.

sources.statement: Sweep slippage assumptions (e.g., 3 to 50 bp) to find the cost level at which the strategy stops being profitable.

rules.title: Sharpe thresholds for strategies
rules.rule: Skip strategies with Sharpe below about 1 or long drawdowns, treat 1–3 as good, higher bars for prop shops, and very high Sharpe as low capacity.

sources.statement: Before backtesting an outside idea, skip strategies with Sharpe below 1 or a maximum drawdown duration of about two years.
Treat Sharpe ratios of 1–3 as good for non-HFT strategies; Sharpe of 5–10 usually means narrow conditions and small capacity.
Prop-shop bar cited: FX strategies should show a Sharpe ratio above 2 and equity strategies about 3 before being considered.

rules.title: Use rolling beta and Sharpe
rules.rule: Judge strategies with rolling beta and rolling Sharpe rather than single summary numbers, since markets are non-stationary.

sources.statement: Judge strategies with rolling beta and rolling Sharpe rather than single summary numbers, because markets are non-stationary.

rules.title: Market-neutral means near-zero exposures
rules.rule: For market-neutral allocations, require beta and factor exposures near zero.

sources.statement: For market-neutral allocations, require beta near zero and near-zero Fama-French factor exposures.

rules.title: Prevent look-ahead bias
rules.rule: Avoid look-ahead bias by using only past data (rolling estimates, no full-sample fits or same-day highs/lows) and verifying truncation does not change earlier positions.

sources.statement: Prevent look-ahead bias: use the same code for backtest and live, and verify that truncating input data does not change earlier positions.
Do not use the day's high or low at the open, or hedge ratios/parameters fitted over the whole period (look-ahead bias).
Avoid subtle look-ahead bias from rolling means/statistics that include future data.
Use rolling estimates (hedge ratio, spread mean, std) computed on returns for pairs trading; a full-sample regression hedge ratio is look-ahead bias.

rules.title: SPY 5/15 SMA close rule
rules.rule: Just before the close, buy SPY if the 5-day SMA is above the 15-day SMA, otherwise sell.

sources.statement: Just before the close, buy SPY if its 5-day moving average is above its 15-day moving average, otherwise sell (platform demo).

rules.title: Being early equals being wrong
rules.rule: Treat alpha as skill in timing, selection and sizing, since being right too early is being wrong.

sources.statement: Alpha is skill at timing selection and sizing; being right too early is the same as being wrong.

rules.title: Model costs from quotes and depth
rules.rule: Model transaction costs from bid/ask quotes and order book size, not a flat assumption.

sources.statement: Model transaction costs using bid/ask quotes and order book size, not a flat assumption.

rules.title: Develop signal, allocation, execution in order
rules.rule: Develop and measure signal, risk allocation and execution separately, not working on execution until the signal is good.

sources.statement: Develop in three separately measured steps: signal (win rate and avg win/avg loss), risk allocation (vs equal-weight benchmark), then trade expression; do not work on execution until the signal is good.

rules.title: High Sharpe from many modest bets
rules.rule: Expect high-Sharpe strategies to win only slightly over half of trades but most days through many independent bets.

sources.statement: High-Sharpe strategies typically win only 51–58% of trades but 60–75% of days by placing many independent bets.

rules.title: Filter out bad trades
rules.rule: Improve simple strategies by adding filters (e.g., a random-forest overlay) that remove bad trades rather than adding complexity.

sources.statement: Improve simple, intuitive strategies by adding filters that remove bad trades rather than adding complexity; subtraction is harder to arbitrage away.
Use a random-forest overlay to filter out bad trades from an existing strategy (example raised Sharpe from ~1.5 to ~3.5).

rules.title: Select pairs by cointegration
rules.rule: Select pairs by cointegration rather than correlation alone.

sources.statement: Select pairs by cointegration (stationary spread around its mean), not correlation alone; correlated prices can have a non-stationary spread.

rules.title: Test on synthetic price series
rules.rule: Test strategies on synthetic series with controlled trend signal-to-noise, especially when history is short.

sources.statement: Test strategies on synthetic price series with a controlled trend signal-to-noise ratio, especially when real history is short (<2 years).

rules.title: Prefer retail-heavy emerging markets
rules.rule: Prefer emerging, retail-dominated markets for higher signal-to-noise and less institutional competition.

sources.statement: Prefer emerging markets (e.g., ~80% retail China) for higher signal-to-noise and less institutional competition.

rules.title: Prefer non-parametric counting signals
rules.rule: Prefer non-parametric counting signals, such as consecutive higher highs, over optimized lookback parameters.

sources.statement: Prefer non-parametric "counting" signals (e.g., consecutive higher highs) over optimized lookback parameters like moving-average lengths.

rules.title: Simulate degraded win rate by reshuffling
rules.rule: Reshuffle trades and simulate a degraded win rate to get the outcome distribution for the next N trades.

sources.statement: Reshuffle trades and simulate a degraded win rate (e.g., 55%) to get the distribution of outcomes for the next N trades.

rules.title: Prefer asymmetric risk-reward
rules.rule: Accept a lower win rate in exchange for wins larger than losses.

sources.statement: Prefer asymmetric risk-reward: accept a lower win rate in exchange for wins larger than losses.

rules.title: Confirm cointegration before pairs trading
rules.rule: Confirm cointegration with ADF or Johansen tests, then buy the underperforming leg and sell the outperforming one.

sources.statement: Pairs trading: confirm cointegration of correlated stocks with ADF or Johansen tests, then buy the underperforming stock and sell the outperforming one.

rules.title: EMA 10/20 crossover
rules.rule: Buy when EMA(10) crosses above EMA(20) and sell when it crosses below.

sources.statement: Hold long while the fast EMA is above the slow EMA and short below; the crossover is a momentum measure.
Demo EMA rule: buy when EMA(10) minus EMA(20) crosses above zero, sell when it crosses below zero.

rules.title: Measure signals by information coefficient
rules.rule: Measure signals by rank correlation with forward returns that survives constraints and execution.

sources.statement: Measure a signal by its information coefficient (Spearman rank correlation with forward returns); it must stay correlated with future returns through constraints and execution.

rules.title: Alpha is residual to known factors
rules.rule: Regress new models or indicators on known factors and existing alphas, counting only the residual as alpha.

sources.statement: Regress a new model's returns on known risk factors and existing alpha models; only the residual is alpha (e.g., a mean-reversion algo that is mostly short-term reversal adds nothing).
Many charting-forum indicators are momentum or mean reversion in disguise; check new indicators against those known factors.

rules.title: Check risk constraints don't kill alpha
rules.rule: Check whether risk-constrained weights drift far from the model's preferred weights.

sources.statement: Check whether risk constraints destroy alpha: if constrained weights move far from the model's preferred weights, the model may not work in a risk-constrained world.

rules.title: Red-candle ES dip buy failed
rules.rule: Do not trade buying daily ES after a red candle with a green-candle, $500 target or $200 stop exit; it lost money over about 1,500 trades in testing from 2003 to 2016.

sources.statement: Tested and failed: on daily ES 2003–2016, buy next bar after a red candle, exit on green candle/$500 target/$200 stop lost $8,651 over ~1,500 trades (33% win rate).

rules.title: Pick lookbacks from a plateau
rules.rule: Do not optimize indicator lookbacks; choose one from a plateau range where many values perform decently and keep it fixed.

sources.statement: Do not optimize indicator lookbacks; choose one from a plateau range where many values perform decently and keep it fixed.

rules.title: Score with bar-level returns
rules.rule: Score strategies with bar-level returns rather than per-trade returns.

sources.statement: Score strategies with bar-level returns (position × next-bar return) rather than per-trade returns for more stable objective functions.

rules.title: Reject obviously overfit results
rules.rule: Reject in-sample results that are obviously overfit, such as 100% win rates or data leaks.

sources.statement: Reject in-sample results that are obviously overfit, e.g., 100% win rate or a future-data leak, before further testing.

rules.title: Crude momentum demo (hypothetical)
rules.rule: Record only, not a rule: a demo crude-oil momentum strategy with a $2,500 stop and a $5,000 target, with illustrative hypothetical results.

sources.statement: Demo crude-oil momentum strategy with a $2,500 stop and a $5,000 profit target (illustrative, hypothetical results).

rules.title: Maintain a strategy pipeline
rules.rule: Assume all strategies decay and keep developing new ones plus risk infrastructure.

sources.statement: All strategies decay; maintain a pipeline of new strategies and invest in risk management and position sizing infrastructure.

rules.title: 8-EMA, SAR and Stochastic trend setup
rules.rule: Go long (or short) when a candle closes above (below) the 8 EMA, SAR is on the matching side and Stochastic confirms, and stay out if any of the three disagrees.

sources.statement: Go long when a bullish candle closes above the 8-day EMA, Parabolic SAR is below the candle, and fast Stochastic crosses above slow Stochastic.
Go short when a bearish candle closes below the 8-day EMA and Parabolic SAR is above the candle, with Stochastic confirmation.
Take the 8-EMA/SAR/Stochastic trend signal only when all three indicators meet their conditions; if any disagrees, treat it as false and stay out.

rules.title: Skip trend signals at Stochastic extremes
rules.rule: Skip longs when Stochastic is above 80 and shorts when it is below 20.

sources.statement: In the 8-EMA/SAR/Stochastic trend setup, skip longs if Stochastic is already above 80 (overbought) and skip shorts if it is below 20 (oversold).

rules.title: Sell before buying when rebalancing
rules.rule: With fixed cash, sequence rebalancing so reductions and sales execute before increases.

sources.statement: With fixed cash, sequence rebalancing orders so existing positions are reduced/sold before new positions are increased.

rules.title: Filtered MA mean reversion
rules.rule: Sell when the 30-day MA is above the 90-day MA and buy when it is below, but only when the gap exceeds one standard deviation.

sources.statement: MA mean reversion: sell when the 30-day MA is above the 90-day MA and buy when below, but only when the gap exceeds one standard deviation (filtered version beat unfiltered).

rules.title: Prefer well-executed standard signals
rules.rule: Prefer a standard signal with good parameters and execution over a novel poorly optimized one.

sources.statement: Prefer a standard signal with well-optimized parameters and good execution over a novel but poorly optimized signal.

rules.title: Use correlation analogs for bias
rules.rule: Correlate the last 20-50 days with every past window and use the average forward path of the top-10 matches as a bias.

sources.statement: Find historical analogs: correlate the last 20-50 days of ES with every past window since 1997 and use the average forward path of the top-10 matches (top-5 too noisy).

rules.title: Confirm analogs with second market
rules.rule: Count an analog period only if a second market also matched, and use the result as a bias combined with discretion, not a signal.

sources.statement: Count an analog period only if a second market (oil, euro, gold, EUR/JPY, bonds) also matched, and treat the result as a bias to combine with discretion, not a short/long signal.

rules.title: Line-of-least-resistance filter
rules.rule: Take longs only when the close is above the high of two days ago, and shorts only when it is below the low of two days ago.

sources.statement: Line-of-least-resistance filter: take longs only if today's close is above the high of two days ago and shorts only if below the low of two days ago (made an optimized SMA system profitable, drawdowns still large).

rules.title: Global 8% stop and 12% target
rules.rule: Apply a global 8% stop loss and 12% profit target to every trade of the automated strategy.

sources.statement: Set a global 8% stop loss and 12% profit target (percent mode) on every trade of the automated strategy.

rules.title: Stops suit trend following, not mean reversion
rules.rule: Use stop losses in trend-following strategies, recognising they are harder to apply to mean reversion.

sources.statement: Use stop losses in trend-following strategies; they are harder to apply in mean-reversion strategies.

rules.title: Prefer low turnover after costs
rules.rule: Prefer low-turnover strategies, since frequent trading often turns zero-cost profits into losses after costs.

sources.statement: Backtest finding: fading EUR/USD hourly after many consecutive same-direction candles looked profitable at zero cost but lost money in-sample with 2 points of cost.
Prefer low-turnover strategies: strategies that enter and exit the market many times tend to score worse after costs.

rules.title: Predict categories with simple voting models
rules.rule: Predict return categories with simple models and vote across several predictions.

sources.statement: In ML trading models, predict return categories (e.g., up/down) instead of exact values, keep models simple, and use voting across several predictions.

rules.title: Detect overfitting via train-test gap
rules.rule: Compare training and test error and reject non-reproducible algorithms.

sources.statement: Detect overfitting by comparing training error with test error (and bagging); reject algorithms whose results are not reproducible across runs.

rules.title: Try ATR filter before HMM
rules.rule: Try a simple ATR volatility regime filter before a complex model, as it can capture most of an HMM's benefit.

sources.statement: Try a simple ATR filter as a volatility regime switch before a complex model; it can deliver about 80% of an HMM regime model's benefit.

rules.title: Fixed pip TP/SL cut drawdown
rules.rule: Consider fixed take-profit and stop-loss levels (e.g. 100 pips on AUD/USD daily) to reduce drawdown.

sources.statement: On the AUD/USD daily ML strategy, adding a 100-pip take profit and a 100-pip stop loss reduced drawdown.

rules.title: 9/24 EMA with RSI 60/40
rules.rule: Go long when 9 EMA > 24 EMA and RSI > 60, short when 9 EMA < 24 EMA and RSI < 40, and exit on the RSI condition.

sources.statement: Go long when 9 EMA > 24 EMA and RSI(14) > 60; go short when 9 EMA < 24 EMA and RSI < 40; exit on the RSI condition alone.

rules.title: Hedge volatility spikes with VIX longs
rules.rule: Hedge a portfolio against volatility spikes with long VIX derivative positions.

sources.statement: Hedge a portfolio against volatility spikes with long positions in VIX derivatives.

rules.title: Bollinger low-volatility breakouts
rules.rule: Use Bollinger Bands to find low-volatility phases and scan for breakouts from them.

sources.statement: Use Bollinger Bands to identify volatility phases and scan for breakouts out of low-volatility phases.

rules.title: Absolute momentum long/short
rules.rule: Go long if price is above its level F periods ago and short otherwise.

sources.statement: Absolute momentum: go long if current price minus the price F periods ago is above zero, otherwise short (F is the only parameter; daily EURUSD example).

rules.title: Reconcile automated systems daily
rules.rule: Monitor automated systems daily, reconciling trades and comparing live with simulated performance.

sources.statement: Monitor automated systems daily: reconcile trades and compare actual live performance against simulated performance.

rules.title: Don't chase short-term winning records
rules.rule: Do not allocate on short-term winning records; use short-term results only to gradually cut allocation.

sources.statement: Don't allocate to strategies/managers on short-term winning records (performance mean-reverts); use short-term results only to gradually cut allocation.

rules.title: Manage risk at portfolio level
rules.rule: Cap positions by ADV share, limit sector exposure, and add strategies only if they lower risk or raise expected return.

sources.statement: Manage risk at portfolio level: cap positions as a share of average daily volume, limit sector exposure, and add a strategy only if it lowers portfolio risk or raises expected return.

rules.title: Don't trust ADF blindly
rules.rule: Do not trust a stationarity test blindly, since periodic mean trends can pass as stationary.

sources.statement: Don't trust a stationarity test (ADF) blindly: a series with a periodic trend in its mean can pass as stationary.

rules.title: Short daily RSI 80
rules.rule: Short when daily RSI hits 80, target the 20-day MA and stop one ATR above entry.

sources.statement: Short when the daily RSI hits 80; take profit at the 20-day moving average (reset daily) and place the stop one ATR above entry.

rules.title: Test discretionary rules on many examples
rules.rule: Check a discretionary rule on at least 10, ideally 20-30, historical examples other than the one it came from before trusting it.

sources.statement: Check a discretionary rule on at least 10, ideally 20-30, historical examples (excluding the one it was derived from) before trusting it.

rules.title: RSI thresholds depend on regime
rules.rule: Adapt RSI overbought/oversold levels to the market and regime rather than using fixed levels like buying at 30.

sources.statement: RSI overbought/oversold levels vary by market and regime (e.g., 30-40 vs 60-80); 'buy at RSI 30' failed in the 2007-08 crash once RSI broke below 30.

rules.title: Avoid repainting smoother signals
rules.rule: Do not use signals from smoothers that revise history, such as kernel regression turning points, because they create look-ahead bias.

sources.statement: Avoid signals from smoothers that revise history (e.g., Gaussian kernel regression turning points): they create look-ahead bias.

rules.title: Use mark-to-market equity curves
rules.rule: Evaluate strategies on a mark-to-market equity curve rather than closed-trade equity so open-trade drawdowns are visible.

sources.statement: Evaluate strategies on a mark-to-market equity curve, not a closed-trade curve, so open-trade drawdowns are visible.

rules.title: Cross-validate on related markets
rules.rule: Test a system on related markets (e.g. other currencies) and gain confidence only if it passes there too.

sources.statement: Cross-validate a system on related markets (e.g., test a currency system on other currencies); passing there raises confidence.

rules.title: Pair negatively correlated algorithms
rules.rule: Pair negatively correlated strategies (e.g. long ES with 10-year notes) to make the package direction agnostic.

sources.statement: Pair a long-only ES algorithm with a 10-year note algorithm (weekly correlation about -0.35) so the package is market-direction agnostic.

rules.title: Same code for research and live
rules.rule: Use the same code for research and live trading to avoid translation errors.

sources.statement: Use the same code for research and live trading; translating research code into production introduces errors.

rules.title: Forecast volatility from historical volatility
rules.rule: Use historical volatility to predict future volatility, such as short-squeeze risk.

sources.statement: Use historical volatility to predict future volatility (e.g., short-squeeze risk in short-interest strategies); nothing better was found.

rules.title: Beware value traps in screens
rules.rule: In valuation screens, avoid stocks cheap for a reason and calendarize and normalize fundamental data.

sources.statement: In valuation screens, beware cheap stocks that are cheap for a reason; calendarize and normalize fundamental data.

rules.title: Trade against less sophisticated competitors
rules.rule: Prefer markets where competitors are less sophisticated, such as manual or less electronic venues.

sources.statement: Prefer markets where competitors are less sophisticated (e.g., manual market making, less electronic venues).

rules.title: Event-study patterns against baseline drift
rules.rule: Test a pattern with an event study that compares average forward returns after signals with baseline drift across asset classes.

sources.statement: Test any pattern with an event study: average forward returns after each signal and compare against the baseline drift across asset classes.

rules.title: Support/resistance no better than random
rules.rule: Do not trust support/resistance lines, because random levels look just as respected and no test shows S/R beats them.

sources.statement: Don't trust support/resistance lines: random levels look equally respected, and no test shows S/R beats random levels.

rules.title: Mean-revert stocks, trend-follow futures
rules.rule: Fade three-sigma days and RSI extremes in stocks, and use channel breakouts in futures.

sources.statement: Fade three-sigma days and RSI extremes in stocks; use channel breakouts in futures, not stocks (asset classes behave differently).

rules.title: Avoid buying 52-week highs
rules.rule: Avoid buying stocks at 52-week highs, which on average lose over the next month.

sources.statement: Avoid buying stocks at 52-week highs; per event study they lose on average over the next month.

rules.title: 12-month momentum hypothesis
rules.rule: Treat the idea that stocks with positive past-year returns keep rising the next month as a hypothesis, and test it on many stocks before trading.

sources.statement: Momentum hypothesis: stocks with positive returns over the past year may keep positive returns over the next month; test on many stocks before trading.

rules.title: Model returns, not price levels
rules.rule: Model returns rather than price levels, because prices are strongly autocorrelated while returns are not.

sources.statement: Forecast returns, not price levels; a price-level model with high R-squared can just copy yesterday's price.
Model returns, not price levels: prices show strong autocorrelation while returns (e.g., monthly wheat futures) show none significant.

rules.title: Test regression residuals
rules.rule: Before trusting regression signals, test residuals for autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson) and heteroskedasticity (Breusch-Pagan).

sources.statement: Before trusting regression-based signals on financial series, test residuals for autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson) and conditional heteroskedasticity (Breusch-Pagan).

rules.title: Discount wide-spread OTM strikes in calibration
rules.rule: When calibrating implied volatility, down-weight out-of-the-money strikes with wide bid-ask spreads, as they produce the largest errors.

sources.statement: When calibrating implied volatility, discount out-of-the-money strikes with wide bid-ask spreads; they produce the largest model errors.

rules.title: Scale features and keep kernels simple
rules.rule: Scale ML features before training and keep kernels simple (e.g. degree 2) to limit overfitting.

sources.statement: Scale ML features before training (e.g., SVM) so no single feature dominates; keep kernels simple (degree 2) to limit overfitting.

rules.title: NQ intraday hour-of-day effects (unproven)
rules.rule: Treat NQ hour-of-day tendencies as unproven, not as a confirmed edge: 11am-noon ET has been the best hour to hold long (p≈0.075), 10-11am ET the worst, and the volatile 9:30 hour made little.

sources.statement: NQ 11am-noon ET was the best hourly long (buy hour start, sell hour end): up 55.4% of days, +$90/contract vs +$12 random, consistent in both sample halves, but p=0.075 (not proven).
NQ 10-11am ET was the worst hour to hold long (−$76/trade); the 9:30 open hour moved most (~160 pts) but made only $5/trade.

rules.title: Split-sample check for parameter winners
rules.rule: When testing many variants, expect about 5% false positives and require any winner to survive an early-versus-late split-sample check.

sources.statement: When testing many parameter variants, expect ~5% false positives (≈60 of 1,200 tests); require any winner to survive a split-sample (early vs late period) check.

rules.title: Correct for multiple comparisons
rules.rule: Apply a multiple-testing correction across all variants and treat a single significant result among several tests as noise until it repeats.

sources.statement: Apply a multiple-testing correction across all variants (timeframes, directions); a raw p<0.05 in one of six tests is not evidence.
Correct for multiple comparisons: with 8 comparisons about a third of runs find one 'significant' result by luck; treat a single pass (e.g. snow days) as noise until it repeats.

rules.title: Flipping a losing signal is not an edge
rules.rule: Do not assume reversing a losing strategy creates a winner; treat the flip as selection bias and retest it on other timeframes and markets after costs.

sources.statement: Reversing a losing strategy does not make a winner: flipped Turtle Soup (fade fresh 20-bar high/low closing back inside, NQ 15m) was p=0.53 vs random and lost after $14/trade costs.
Flipping the direction of a losing signal is selection bias: picking the loser to flip flatters the result; retest the flipped rule on other timeframes/markets.

rules.title: Index rotation by last month is noise
rules.rule: Do not rotate into last month's best of NQ/ES/YM, as it does not beat a random pick.

sources.statement: Rotating into last month's best index among NQ/ES/YM (long open-to-close daily) made 0.57%/month vs 0.52% for a random pick (p=0.80); daily differences between the three were noise.

rules.title: Overlapping returns are not independent
rules.rule: Treat overlapping daily-start return samples as clustered streaks, not independent observations.

sources.statement: Overlapping daily-start returns cluster into a few streaks (91 NQ all-time-high entry days formed only 4 streaks), so they are not independent samples.

rules.title: Judge rare signals against base rate
rules.rule: Compare rare signal outcomes with the unconditional base rate and do not accept results from a tiny sample of trades.

sources.statement: Judge rare signals against the base rate: daily golden cross fired twice in 5 years and NQ rose both times, but NQ rises in 63% of 20-session stretches anyway; two trades prove nothing.

rules.title: Big NQ range days cluster, not direction
rules.rule: Expect big-range NQ days to be followed by more big-range days, but do not infer next-day direction from them.

sources.statement: Big-range NQ days cluster: after a top-20% range day (≥2.6% range), 48% of next days were big vs 20% base (35% vs 12% excluding 2022); shuffles never matched.
A big-range NQ day does not predict the next day's direction: up 57% after big days vs 53% after normal days (p=0.46).

rules.title: Test data-mined strategies once on unseen data
rules.rule: Test genetic or data-mined strategies a single time on fresh unseen data and compare survivors against the number expected by chance.

sources.statement: Genetic-algorithm/data-mined strategies must be tested once on unseen data: 163 survivors of 4.6M bred FX strategies (EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY, 30m-4h) were 43% profitable on a fresh year; 13 beat random vs ~8 by chance.

rules.title: Buying after red streaks is weak, fading
rules.rule: Do not rely on buying NQ after 3+ consecutive red days, as the edge is not significant and has more than halved recently.

sources.statement: After 3 consecutive red NQ days, buy the next open and sell the close: +$1,175 vs +$264 random day (4 red: $1,500; 5 red: $3,000) but p=0.09 and the edge more than halved in the last 2 years.

rules.title: NQ Monday long effect
rules.rule: Consider the NQ Monday effect, where buying the full-session open and selling the close on Mondays has been significantly profitable (p≈0.002) while other weekdays lost on average.

sources.statement: Monday effect on NQ: buying the full-session open (overnight included) and selling the close on Mondays made $1,190/contract, up 61% of Mondays, p=0.002, stronger in last 2 years ($1,675); Tue/Thu/Fri lost on average.

rules.title: Session return leadership flips
rules.rule: Do not assume overnight or regular session carries NQ returns, since leadership flips over time.

sources.statement: NQ return leadership between overnight (6pm-9:30) and regular session (9:30-4pm) flips over time (overnight +42% vs RTH +30% over 5 years, p=0.94); don't assume one session carries the returns.

rules.title: Selling after green streaks has no edge
rules.rule: Do not sell NQ after 5 consecutive green days, as the result is insignificant and flips with session definition.

sources.statement: Selling after 5 consecutive green NQ days has no edge: next full-session day +$1,110 vs +$264 random (57 trades, p=0.08), but RTH-only it flips to −$70; result depends on session definition.

rules.title: Do not wait for a dip to invest
rules.rule: Invest now rather than waiting for a dip, since waiting does not help and deeper dip thresholds often never trigger.

sources.statement: Waiting for a dip before investing in NQ doesn't help: waiting for a 10% dip matched buying day one (+73% vs +74%); demanding 15% meant it never came 28% of the time and cost 14 points of return.

rules.title: Best and worst days cluster together
rules.rule: Do not over-read the 'missing the best days' statistic, because best and worst days cluster in the same bad years and removing both leaves returns nearly unchanged.

sources.statement: Missing the 10 best NQ days cuts returns sharply, but best and worst days cluster in the same bad years; removing both the 10 best and 10 worst left returns nearly unchanged (+98% vs +101%).

rules.title: Daily momentum on NQ has no edge
rules.rule: Do not buy NQ after rising stretches of any lookback, as daily momentum did not beat random.

sources.statement: Daily momentum on NQ (buy after a rising stretch, lookbacks 5 days to 1 year) beat random in none of 6 lookbacks (best p=0.52); buying after falling stretches did as well or better.

rules.title: Reject lunar phase filters
rules.rule: Do not use lunar phase (full or new moon) as a session filter, because its apparent effect is noise.

sources.statement: Lunar phase (full/new moon) as an NQ session filter is noise: full moon +$1,265 vs +$199 other days (p=0.08) and new moon was similar.

rules.title: Adjust significance for best-of selection
rules.rule: When picking the best of several variants, expect it to look good by luck alone and adjust significance for the selection.

sources.statement: When choosing the best of several variants (e.g. 3 sessions), expect the winner to land near the 75th percentile of random by luck alone; adjust significance for selection.

rules.title: Efficiency ratio too weak to trade
rules.rule: Treat yesterday's efficiency ratio as only weak, untradeable context for whether today trends.

sources.statement: Yesterday's efficiency ratio weakly predicts the opposite today on NQ: after the most trending third of days 44% of next days trended above normal vs 54% after the choppiest; p=0.001 but <1% explained, too weak to trade.

rules.title: Separate execution from trade checking
rules.rule: Never let a trader both execute trades and verify their own positions.

sources.statement: Separate trade execution from trade checking: no trader should run both the desk and the back office that verifies their own positions (Barings/Leeson).

rules.title: Drawdowns recover but unscheduled
rules.rule: Expect NQ 5%+ drawdowns to usually recover, but not on any reliable schedule.

sources.statement: NQ 5%+ drawdowns from a closing high: 9 of 10 recovered since 2021, median ~63 trading days, but the 35% 2022 drop took 533 trading days; expect recovery but not on a schedule.

rules.title: Post-hoc regime splits are leads only
rules.rule: Treat a regime split chosen after seeing results as a hypothesis to test, not a finding.

sources.statement: Treat a regime split chosen after seeing results as a lead, not a finding (double top: 2021-23 +$46/trade vs 2024+ -$79/trade).

rules.title: Check the parameter fitness landscape
rules.rule: Sweep all parameter combinations and reject strategies that sit on a cliff edge where small changes collapse performance.

sources.statement: Sweep all parameter combinations and check the fitness landscape: a strategy on a cliff edge (stop 2.0 ATR -> 2.6 ATR drops Sharpe 3.17 -> 1.53) is fragile.

rules.title: Buy NQ 50-day closing lows (thin sample)
rules.rule: Consider buying NQ at a 50-day closing low and holding 20 days, but treat it as tentative because there were only about 10 independent selloffs.

sources.statement: Buy NQ at the close of a 50-day closing low and hold 20 trading days: +3.0% vs +1.2% random (p=0.011, 67% win) and both halves beat random, but only 10 independent selloffs; 20-day lows were inside random.

rules.title: Use call calendars for medium-term bullishness
rules.rule: When bullish on a stock for about three months to two years, use a long call calendar spread instead of shares or a long call.

sources.statement: Use a long call calendar spread, not shares or a long call, when you are bullish on a stock for roughly three months to two years.

rules.title: Build same-strike calendar from intended call
rules.rule: Build a calendar by selling the call you would have bought and buying the same strike in a later expiry.

sources.statement: Build the calendar from the call you would have bought: sell that call, then buy the same strike in the expiry with about twice the time.
Use the same strike on both legs of the calendar.

rules.title: Long leg about double short leg DTE
rules.rule: Set the calendar's long-leg days to expiry at about twice the short leg's, using the nearest available chain.
