sources.statement: Set the long leg's days to expiry at about double the short leg's (e.g. 161 DTE short, about 320 DTE long; take the nearest available chain).

rules.title: Sell short-dated calls against a LEAP
rules.rule: Instead of holding a LEAP outright, sell short-dated (e.g. 30 DTE) same-strike calls against it and re-sell a new one after each expires, to offset cost and collect time decay.

sources.statement: Instead of holding a LEAP outright, sell a short-dated call at the same strike against it to offset part of its cost and gain a time-decay edge.
Variant: buy a long-dated call (about 380 DTE) and sell a 30-DTE call at the same strike, re-selling a new short leg each month after the front leg expires.

rules.title: Earnings calendar instead of weekly
rules.rule: For earnings, sell the option expiring in earnings week and buy the same strike expiring the week after, instead of buying the weekly outright.

sources.statement: For an earnings play, sell the option expiring in earnings week and buy the same strike in the chain expiring the week after earnings, instead of buying the weekly outright.

rules.title: IV crush after earnings
rules.rule: Expect implied volatility to fall after earnings, eroding outright options and shrinking calendar max profit.

sources.statement: Do not buy earnings-week calls or puts outright: implied volatility drops after the report and IV crush erodes the option even if the stock moves.
Expect an earnings calendar's graph max profit to shrink after the report, because implied volatility falls on both legs.

rules.title: Take calendar profit at strike cross
rules.rule: Take profit on a calendar spread once the stock price crosses the strike.

sources.statement: Take profit on a calendar once the stock price crosses the strike.

rules.title: Hold calendar between break-evens
rules.rule: Hold a calendar spread while the stock trades between its break-even points so short-leg decay adds profit.

sources.statement: Hold the calendar while the stock trades between the two break-even points; time decay of the short leg adds profit there.

rules.title: Leave 10-15% downside break-even buffer
rules.rule: Choose calendar strikes and expiries so the lower break-even sits about 10-15% below price.

sources.statement: Choose calendar strikes and expiries so the lower break-even sits about 10-15% below the current price, leaving a downside buffer.

rules.title: Never trade with living money
rules.rule: Keep living savings separate from the trading account and never trade rent money.

sources.statement: Keep living savings separate from the trading account; never trade with rent money.

rules.title: Go full-time only with a cushion
rules.rule: Do not go full-time until a bad month would not break you.

sources.statement: Do not go full-time until a bad month would not break you.

rules.title: Strategy must survive chop and crashes
rules.rule: Judge a strategy by whether it survives choppy markets and crashes, not by one good year.

sources.statement: Judge a strategy by whether it survives choppy markets and crashes, not by one good year.

rules.title: Avoid outright option buying by default
rules.rule: Avoid buying options outright by default because of time decay, and prefer structures that are short the faster-decaying option.

sources.statement: Avoid buying options outright as a default, because they lose value every day to time decay; prefer structures where you are short the faster-decaying option.

rules.title: Skip credit spreads for directional upside
rules.rule: Do not use credit spreads when you want directional upside, since they risk a lot to make a little and cap the move.

sources.statement: Skip credit spreads when you want directional upside: they risk a lot to make a little and cap the move.

rules.title: No covered calls on keep-and-grow stocks
rules.rule: Do not sell covered calls or run the wheel on high-conviction stocks where you want full upside or to keep accumulating, because assignment caps the move.

sources.statement: Do not sell covered calls on high-conviction stocks you want to keep accumulating.
Do not sell covered calls or run the wheel if you want the full upside: assignment or a capped short call misses the move.

rules.title: Buy bull flag breakout
rules.rule: Buy a bull flag when price breaks out of the flag after an up move.

sources.statement: Buy a bull flag when price breaks out of the flag after a move up.

rules.title: Sell failed flag breakout
rules.rule: If a bull-flag breakout falls back into the flag, sell and take the small loss.

sources.statement: If a bull-flag breakout falls back into the flag, sell and take the small loss.

rules.title: Weekly flipped support plus golden cross
rules.rule: Treat weekly resistance turned support plus a golden cross as a bullish setup for a call calendar.

sources.statement: On the weekly chart, treat old resistance that has turned into support plus a golden cross as a bullish setup for a call calendar.

rules.title: Undercut and rip entry
rules.rule: Enter when price briefly breaks below support and then reverses back up.

sources.statement: Look for an undercut and rip below support (a brief break under support that reverses) as an entry signal.

rules.title: Fade outer band touches with confirmation
rules.rule: Treat an outer band touch as support/resistance with likely reversion to mid-range, buy lower-band touches, and confirm with RSI or MACD.

sources.statement: With his (unnamed) band indicator, treat a touch of the outer band as support/resistance with likely reversion to mid-range, a touch of the lower band as a buy signal, and confirm with RSI or MACD.

rules.title: Read support with volume
rules.rule: Read support levels together with traded volume to anticipate moves.

sources.statement: Read support levels together with traded volume to anticipate moves.

rules.title: Uncertainty rotates into gold
rules.rule: In times of uncertainty, expect money to rotate into gold.

sources.statement: In times of uncertainty expect money to rotate into gold (GLD).

rules.title: Stay disciplined with a feedback loop
rules.rule: Once live, stick to your own rules and keep improving in a loop: analyse, change, test, repeat.

sources.statement: Once live, stay disciplined to your own rules and keep a feedback loop: analyse results, change, test, repeat.

rules.title: Price is the primary signal
rules.rule: Treat price action, such as breaks above resistance or losses of support, as the main signal and other indicators as secondary.

sources.statement: Treat price itself (breaks above resistance, losses of support) as the primary signal; other indicators are secondary.

rules.title: Never FOMO into trades
rules.rule: Never chase a trade after it has run or because someone else bought it.

sources.statement: Never FOMO into a trade after it has already run or because someone else bought it.

rules.title: Use limit orders, not market orders
rules.rule: Use limit orders rather than market orders, especially on wide-spread options.

sources.statement: Use limit orders, never market orders, especially on options with wide bid-ask spreads.

rules.title: Mostly technicals, check events for swings
rules.rule: Weight analysis about 90% technicals and 10% fundamentals, but check fundamentals and upcoming events like earnings for swing trades.

sources.statement: Weight analysis about 90% technicals and 10% fundamentals, but for swings check fundamentals and upcoming events such as earnings.

rules.title: Trade from a personal watchlist
rules.rule: Trade from a personal watchlist with price alerts at buy levels, and drop names under $10.

sources.statement: Trade off a personal watchlist: scan it and set price alerts at buy levels; drop names under $10.

rules.title: Never marry a position
rules.rule: Take profits rather than holding a favourite stock indefinitely.

sources.statement: Never marry a stock or position; take profits instead of holding a favourite indefinitely.

rules.title: Hold through earnings only with cushion
rules.rule: Hold through earnings only if the position already shows about 10% profit or more than the expected move.

sources.statement: Do not hold through earnings unless the position already shows about 10% profit (or more than the expected move).

rules.title: Aim for the middle of the move
rules.rule: Aim to capture the middle of a move rather than the exact top or bottom.

sources.statement: Aim for the middle of the move, not the exact top or bottom.

rules.title: Concentrate on 6-8 known stocks
rules.rule: Focus on about 6-8 stocks you know well, and add more only after mastering their levels.

sources.statement: Concentrate on a basket of about 6-8 stocks you know well, and add one or two only after mastering their levels.

rules.title: Buy support, sell resistance
rules.rule: Buy at support and sell at resistance using levels marked in advance.

sources.statement: Buy at support and sell at resistance using levels marked in advance.

rules.title: News confirms technicals
rules.rule: Use news to confirm the technicals rather than to lead, since mainstream news usually arrives too late.

sources.statement: Let news confirm the technicals, not the other way around; by the time it is mainstream news it is too late.

rules.title: Use wider stops on longer options
rules.rule: For options two or more weeks out, use about a 50% stop or a smaller position instead of a tight 20% stop.

sources.statement: For options two or more weeks out, avoid a tight 20% stop: use about 50%, or take a smaller position and let it work.

rules.title: Take only clean stacked squeezes
rules.rule: With the TTM Squeeze, enter only clean, stacked setups.

sources.statement: With the TTM Squeeze, enter only clean, stacked setups.

rules.title: TTM Squeeze move lasts 6-8 candles
rules.rule: After a TTM Squeeze fires, expect the move to last about 6-8 candles.

sources.statement: After a TTM Squeeze fires, expect the move to last about 6-8 candles.

rules.title: Full size only with aligned trends
rules.rule: Take a full position only when the stock, its sector ETF and the market all trend in the same direction.

sources.statement: Take a full position only when the stock, its sector ETF and the market all trend the same way.

rules.title: Fund lotto options from weekly profits
rules.rule: Buy speculative lotto options only with a small part of profits already made that week.

sources.statement: Play lotto options only with profits already made that week, and only a small part of them.

rules.title: Trade only RS leaders in uptrend
rules.rule: Trade only stocks with an RS rating of about 97+, a rising RS line, and the S&P 500 in an uptrend.

sources.statement: Trade only stocks with a relative strength rating of about 97 or higher, a rising RS line and the S&P 500 in an uptrend.

rules.title: Buy higher low, stop below it
rules.rule: Buy a higher low in an uptrend and stop out if price breaks the prior higher low.

sources.statement: Buy at a higher low in an uptrend and stop out if price breaks the prior higher low.

rules.title: Hold hot trends one to three days
rules.rule: For hot, high-relative-strength trends, plan to hold about one to three days and then step off.

sources.statement: For hot, high-RS trends, plan to hold about one to three days and then step off.

rules.title: Buy pullbacks near key EMAs
rules.rule: On low-volume pullbacks, buy only within about 1-2% of the 10, 20 or 50-day EMA.

sources.statement: On a low-volume pullback, buy only when price is within about 1-2% of the 10, 20 or 50-day EMA.

rules.title: Wait for pullback to cut entry risk
rules.rule: Skip entries needing about 6% risk to the stop and wait for a pullback cutting risk to about 3%.

sources.statement: Skip entries whose stop (e.g. prior day's low) would mean about 6% risk; wait for a pullback that cuts risk to about 3%.

rules.title: Wait for 5-day MA to turn up
rules.rule: Do not buy while the 5-day MA is falling, and wait for it to flatten and turn up.

sources.statement: Do not buy while the 5-day moving average is trending down; wait for it to flatten and turn up.

rules.title: Buy first 50 EMA tap after earnings gap
rules.rule: After a 7%+ earnings gap on heavy volume, buy the first tap of the 50-day EMA.

sources.statement: After a power earnings gap (up 7% or more on very heavy volume), look to buy the first tap of the 50-day EMA.

rules.title: Favour early-stage base breakouts
rules.rule: Favour the first two breakouts from a major base, because later bases are less reliable.

sources.statement: Favour the first two breakouts from a major base; later bases are less reliable.

rules.title: Stop below pivot or higher low
rules.rule: When buying a pivot breakout, place the stop below the pivot line or the last higher low.

sources.statement: When buying a pivot breakout, stop out below the pivot line or below the last higher low.

rules.title: VCP needs drying volume
rules.rule: Require a contraction with drying-up volume before buying a VCP breakout.

sources.statement: For a VCP, require a contraction with drying-up volume before buying the breakout.

rules.title: Enter through prior day high
rules.rule: After a low-volume pullback, enter as price trades through the prior day's high.

sources.statement: After a low-volume pullback, enter as price trades through the prior day's high.

rules.title: Downtrend bounces are relief only
rules.rule: Once structure breaks and the trend is down, treat bounces as relief bounces, not new uptrends.

sources.statement: Once structure breaks and the trend is down, treat bounces as relief bounces, not new uptrends.

rules.title: Stagger buys in thirds
rules.rule: Stagger buys in thirds across a demand zone to improve the average price.

sources.statement: Stagger buys in thirds across a demand zone to build a better average price.

rules.title: Prefer buying demand zones
rules.rule: Prefer buying in demand zones, where the exit is clear and downside risk is smallest.

sources.statement: Prefer buying in demand zones, where the exit is clear and downside risk is smallest.

rules.title: Demand zones at 0.5-0.618 retracement
rules.rule: Mark demand zones at the 0.5-0.618 retracement of the prior swing and confirm with other tools.

sources.statement: Mark demand zones at the 0.5-0.618 retracement of the prior swing, with other tools for confirmation.

rules.title: Strength buyers use reclaims and breaks
rules.rule: If you buy strength, enter on a 21 EMA reclaim or a break of major resistance rather than buying dips.

sources.statement: If you are a strength buyer, enter on a reclaim of the 21 EMA or a break of major resistance instead of buying dips.

rules.title: Covered call strikes 5-20% OTM
rules.rule: Sell covered calls about 5-20% out of the money and never more than 30%.

sources.statement: Sell covered calls about 5-20% out of the money, never more than 30%.

rules.title: Sell covered calls into strength
rules.rule: Time covered call sales into bouts of strength, such as after an explosive up day.

sources.statement: Sell covered calls into bouts of strength, after an explosive up day.

rules.title: Open interest is not direction
rules.rule: Do not read high open interest as direction, since it doesn't show whether contracts were bought or sold.

sources.statement: High open interest alone does not show whether contracts were bought or sold; do not read it as direction.

rules.title: Ignore options flow you can't read
rules.rule: Ignore options flow if it is too hard to interpret.

sources.statement: If options flow is too hard to interpret, ignore it.

rules.title: Judge catalysts by quality
rules.rule: Rate catalysts by quality: weak ones such as a single upgrade fade, while strong ones last.

sources.statement: Judge catalysts by quality: weak catalysts such as a single upgrade fade, strong ones last.

rules.title: Assume speculative firms may dilute
rules.rule: Always assume a share offering is possible with speculative companies.

sources.statement: With speculative companies, always assume a share offering is possible.

rules.title: More pivots mean stronger level
rules.rule: Treat a support or resistance level as stronger the more past pivots it intersects.

sources.statement: A support or resistance level is stronger the more past pivots it intersects.

rules.title: Keep starter positions small
rules.rule: Keep starter positions around 3.5-5% so failures are small while winners still matter.

sources.statement: Keep starter positions small (about 3.5-5%) so a failed breakout is a paper cut while a winner still moves the portfolio.

rules.title: New traders follow stop rules strictly
rules.rule: Follow stop rules strictly as a new trader; only experienced traders should allow a strong name a small cushion past the risk point.

sources.statement: New traders must follow their stop rules; only experienced traders may give a strong name a small cushion past the risk point.

rules.title: Post-earnings drop means bad earnings
rules.rule: If a stock falls after earnings you thought were good, accept that the market judged them not good.

sources.statement: If a stock falls after earnings you thought were good, the market judged them not good.

rules.title: Buy options below about 75% IV
rules.rule: When buying options, generally choose contracts with implied volatility below about 75%, and lower for low-beta names.

sources.statement: When buying options, generally buy contracts below about 75% implied volatility (lower for low-beta names).

rules.title: Watch technicals on new positions only
rules.rule: Monitor technical health such as 21 EMA breaks for new positions, not long-term holdings.

sources.statement: Monitor technical health (e.g. 21 EMA breaks) for recently opened positions; long-term holdings need not react to it.

rules.title: Sell cyclicals at obvious peak earnings
rules.rule: Sell cyclical stocks when peak earnings become obvious.

sources.statement: Sell cyclical stocks when peak earnings become obvious.

rules.title: Weigh debt more when unprofitable
rules.rule: Take debt and liabilities far more seriously when the operating business is unprofitable.

sources.statement: Take debt and liabilities far more seriously when the operating business is unprofitable.

rules.title: Quiet consolidation above MAs is constructive
rules.rule: Read sideways consolidation above the moving averages on falling volume as a lack of sellers.

sources.statement: Read sideways consolidation above the moving averages on falling volume as a lack of sellers (constructive).

rules.title: Look beyond Sharpe ratio
rules.rule: Do not rely on Sharpe alone; check Sortino and Calmar because high Sharpe can hide short-volatility tail risk.

sources.statement: Do not rely on the Sharpe ratio alone; check Sortino and Calmar because high-Sharpe strategies can hide short-volatility tail risk.

rules.title: Add strategy if Sharpe beats correlation hurdle
rules.rule: Add a new strategy only if its Sharpe exceeds its correlation times the current portfolio Sharpe, noting negatively correlated strategies can help even when losing.

sources.statement: Add a new strategy only if its Sharpe exceeds the correlation times your current Sharpe; negatively correlated strategies can help even when they lose money.

rules.title: Use GARCH volatility, not static estimates
rules.rule: Expect volatility to stay elevated after shocks and use a GARCH-type (e.g. Student-t) forecast instead of constant volatility or historical-simulation VaR.

sources.statement: Expect volatility to stay elevated for weeks after a shock; use a GARCH-type forecast instead of constant volatility.
Do not use historical-simulation VaR after a crash; a GARCH model with Student-t errors adapts while historical VaR keeps missing.

rules.title: Validate with combinatorial purged cross-validation
rules.rule: Use combinatorial purged cross-validation with purging and embargo to get a distribution of Sharpe ratios rather than one path.

sources.statement: Validate with combinatorial purged cross-validation (purge overlapping labels, embargo) to get a distribution of Sharpe ratios rather than one path.

rules.title: 12-month time-series momentum filter
rules.rule: Stay long when price is above its level 12 months ago and step out when below, acting on the prior day's signal to avoid lookahead.

sources.statement: Stay long when price is above its level 12 months ago and step out when below, trading on yesterday's signal to avoid lookahead.

rules.title: Trade 20-day Donchian breakouts
rules.rule: Go long on a close above the 20-day high and go flat or short on a close below the 20-day low.

sources.statement: Go long on a close above the 20-day high and go flat or short on a close below the 20-day low (Donchian breakout).

rules.title: Z-score mean-reversion entry
rules.rule: Buy when the price z-score versus its rolling mean falls below -2 and sell when it reverts to 0, treating this as a hypothesis to test.

sources.statement: Buy when the price z-score versus its rolling mean falls below -2 and sell when it reverts to 0; treat as a hypothesis to test, not proof.

rules.title: Cut momentum when crowding is high
rules.rule: Reduce momentum exposure when comomentum is in its top quintile, as subsequent momentum returns fall sharply.

sources.statement: Reduce momentum exposure when comomentum (crowding) is in its top quintile; momentum returns fall sharply over the next two years.

rules.title: Exit on falling bull-regime probability
rules.rule: Exit when the filtered probability of the bull regime drops below a threshold rather than at fixed price targets.

sources.statement: Exit when the filtered probability of the bull regime drops below a threshold rather than at fixed price targets.

rules.title: Clean covariance before optimising
rules.rule: Clean the covariance matrix with shrinkage or eigenvalue clipping before optimising, since most estimated entries are noise.

sources.statement: Clean the covariance matrix (shrinkage, eigenvalue clipping) before optimising; most estimated entries are noise.

rules.title: Optimised portfolios understate realised risk
rules.rule: Expect an optimised portfolio's realised risk to exceed predicted risk by roughly 1/(1 - n/T).

sources.statement: Expect an optimised portfolio's realised risk to exceed its predicted risk by roughly 1/(1 - n/T).

rules.title: Default to equal weighting
rules.rule: Default to equal weighting unless you have very long data histories, because estimation error wipes out mean-variance gains.

sources.statement: Default to equal weighting unless you have centuries of data; estimation error wipes out mean-variance gains.

rules.title: Diversification fails in crises
rules.rule: Do not count on diversification in a crisis, since correlations spike in downturns and the correlation floor cannot be diversified away.

sources.statement: Do not count on diversification in a crisis; correlations spike in downturns and the correlation floor cannot be diversified away.

rules.title: Shrink betas toward the mean
rules.rule: Shrink measured betas toward the cross-sectional mean before use, because extreme betas mean-revert.

sources.statement: Shrink measured betas toward the cross-sectional mean before using them; extreme betas mean-revert.

rules.title: Hedge short calls with higher volatility
rules.rule: When hedging a short call, use a hedging volatility above realised volatility at every instant to cover the payoff on every path.

sources.statement: When hedging a short call, use a hedging volatility above the market's realised volatility at every instant to cover the payoff on every path.

rules.title: Post-earnings drift gone in large caps
rules.rule: Do not assume post-earnings drift persists in large caps, as recent earnings surprises have not predicted drift from day 2 to day 60.

sources.statement: Do not assume post-earnings drift persists in large caps; since 2006 surprises have not predicted drift from day 2 to day 60.

rules.title: Debate outcome X01
rules.rule: Scale in only when total size, add levels and one never-lowered invalidation level are fixed before the first entry. Adding because the price is lower is averaging down.

rules.title: Debate outcome X02
rules.rule: Every position has a stop at its invalidation level from entry, and size is set from that distance. For long options the premium is the maximum loss, so size the premium as if the stop will gap.

rules.title: Debate outcome X03
rules.rule: Default to defined-risk structures (debit spreads, credit spreads, long options, cash-secured puts). No undefined-risk short premium.

rules.title: Debate outcome X05
rules.rule: A stop is not a maximum-loss limit; position size is the real control. Keep per-name concentration inside the owner caps.

rules.title: Debate outcome X06
rules.rule: Do not pre-position for a post-event move (FOMC, CPI, earnings). Going flat is not the default either: size every open position so an event gap through the stop is affordable.

rules.title: Debate outcome X07
rules.rule: Do not use margin to buy dips. Options premium is paid in cash and capped per name.

rules.title: Debate outcome X09
rules.rule: Require at least 2:1 reward to risk by default. Lower it for a setup only when the lower confidence bound of its logged hit rate supports the lower ratio.

rules.title: Debate outcome X10
rules.rule: Do not commit full size at an apparent bottom. Stage entries and wait for confirmation before the full position.

rules.title: Debate outcome X11
rules.rule: An extended or parabolic move alone is not a trigger to fade it. Wait for a confirmed reversal.

rules.title: Debate outcome X12
rules.rule: Neither blind mechanical trailing nor a never-touch rule: trail only to plan levels (structure, not ticks or ATR alone) and record each change.
